result.topic_en: Euler argues that the forces drawing terrestrial bodies toward the Sun and Moon cannot come from a continual impulse of subtle matter and must come from centrifugal force. He places the proximate cause of the tides in two vortices of subtle matter, one around the Sun and one around the Moon, whose centrifugal forces fall off as the inverse square of distance.

items.english: But a hypothesis of this kind (subtle matter continually rushing toward the Sun and Moon) can by no means be admitted, because of the very great difficulties in which it is involved.

items.english: We therefore place the proximate cause of the ebb and flow of the sea in two vortices of a certain subtle matter, one revolving about the Sun and the other about the Moon, such that in each the centrifugal forces decrease in the duplicate ratio (as the square) of the distances from the centre of the vortex.
